outcome_detail: Clark County officials agreed on April 11, 2024 to pay $328,000 to settle the claims of 25 former detainees across the related federal suits (Coomer v. Lowe, No. 4:22-cv-00079; Hill v. Maples, No. 4:23-cv-00033; Doe 4 v. Maples, No. 4:23-cv-00034, all S.D. Ind.); per Prison Legal News, 15 plaintiffs received $10,000 each and the remaining 10 received up to $25,000 each, with attorney fees paid from the settlement. Local reporting in early April 2024 said the settlements were confidential and that the final plaintiff settled in March 2024; the county's liability insurance carrier handled litigation and settlement costs.
criminal_detail: Jail officer David Lowe was arrested in October 2021 and charged with aiding an escape, official misconduct, and trafficking with an inmate. In February 2025, a Clark County Circuit Court judge dismissed the case; prosecutor Jeremy Mull said that after reviewing all the evidence he was 'less than certain' Lowe was guilty. Separately, former Sheriff Jamey Noel pleaded guilty on August 27, 2024 to corruption charges unrelated to the jail assaults (including theft, official misconduct, corrupt business influence, money laundering, obstruction of justice, and tax evasion) and was sentenced to 12 years plus 3 years of probation.
incident_date_approx: Night of October 23-24, 2021, Clark County Jail, Jeffersonville, Indiana
description: Twenty-eight women who had been detained at the Clark County Jail sued then-Sheriff Jamey Noel, jail officer David Lowe, and other current and former jail employees in federal court in the Southern District of Indiana, in suits filed in June and July 2022 with related cases filed in 2023. The suits allege that on the night of October 23-24, 2021, Lowe accepted $1,000 from male detainees for access to jail keys, and that men from the male side of the jail, some wearing masks made from towels and blankets, entered the women's housing pods where, according to the complaints, women were raped, assaulted, harassed, threatened, and intimidated for several hours while no officer on duty intervened despite surveillance cameras covering the area. The complaints also allege some women were punished after reporting the incident. The county agreed in April 2024 to pay $328,000 to settle the claims of 25 plaintiffs. Criminal charges against Lowe (aiding an escape, official misconduct, and trafficking with an inmate) were dismissed in February 2025.
notes: Direct perpetrators of the alleged assaults were male detainees; the officers, sheriff, and county were sued for enabling the attack and failing to intervene. Aggregate reporting: the litigation comprised multiple filings (June 2022 suit by 20 women; July 22, 2022 suit by 8 women; related federal cases Coomer v. Lowe 4:22-cv-00079, Hill v. Maples 4:23-cv-00033, and Doe 4 v. Maples 4:23-cv-00034) settled together for $328,000 covering 25 plaintiffs, so this is kept as one record with multiple_filings=true.

confidence_notes: Settlement figures conflict slightly across sources: Prison Legal News reports $328,000 settled April 11, 2024 covering 25 plaintiffs (15 at $10,000 each, 10 at up to $25,000 each), while Louisville Public Media (April 4, 2024) said amounts were confidential under NDAs with the final plaintiff settling in March 2024; the PLN figure and date are used per the seed. 28 women filed suit in 2022 but the settlement is reported as covering 25 plaintiffs; the discrepancy is unexplained in coverage. Filing structure is complex (June 2022 and July 2022 suits reported in media; PLN lists three federal case numbers spanning 2022-2023), so year_filed=2022 with filing_year_range 2022-2023 and multiple_filings=true. Sheriff Noel's guilty plea was to corruption charges unrelated to the assault claims; no one was criminally convicted in connection with the jail breach itself after Lowe's charges were dismissed in February 2025.
